witness_requirements: The parent retains separate conditions that the assessed event is an actual STR submission and that evidence from separate attempts is not combined; the children do not execute or preserve the event-level evidence-separation condition.

The parent limits footnote 3 to the XML and prescribed-PDF alternatives; the children leave this as an unresolved source-boundary issue, so the executable relation does not preserve that scope condition.

The parent separately excludes XML-schema conformity, technical testing, reporting timeliness, substantive STR adequacy, and overall legal compliance from the selected decision; those limitations are omitted from the executable children.

The parent retains blackout urgent-contact and post-implementation resubmission distinctions, including that resubmission does not alter the original event’s channel or time; the children do not execute these conditions.

The parent states that no event-level truth value is assigned because the certificate relationship is unresolved. The child statement preserves that unresolved issue, but the resulting child set cannot evaluate the broader parent proposition with all of its stated conditions.

No executable preservation is demonstrated: the sole child has null formalization and is UNENCODED with E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE. Actor, filing-event scope, temporal scope, method alternatives, certificate attachment and unknown-value handling survive only in prose.
The parent expression uses undeclared is_xml_submission. Neither that defect nor the missing XML schema is resolved by the proposal.
The certificate requirement remains attached only to XML and prescribed PDF, without an added web-form requirement; its operational satisfaction conditions remain unspecified.
Equating implementation with the inclusive 9:00am launch boundary remains an interpretation. The date-level effective provision and the unspecified timezone are not conclusively resolved.

Blackout urgent contact and mandatory resubmission after an off-channel filing remain prose residuals, not executable obligations. A later compliant filing cannot by itself establish discharge of a particular earlier filing's resubmission duty.
The XML technical-test liaison duty is outside the selected filing control in both versions; neither version establishes compliance with that separate source obligation.
The children narrow the actor from the parent’s general STR context to licensed firms, matching the cited SFC circular but adding a scope condition not explicit in the parent statement.

The contact child restates the blackout with exact intraday boundaries and frames the trigger as each STR requiring urgent submission; the source does not define urgency or establish that contact completes filing.

The history child adds the separate express re-submission obligation for post-implementation submissions through other channels. This is properly bounded and does not assert that blackout contact itself is a submission, but it adds a conditional rule beyond the parent’s original wording.

The executable bundle adds valid_from = 2026-09-26, after the entire blackout. Preservation requires an explicit distinction between bundle-version validity and the historical instant being assessed; none is supplied.

Urgency is tested at the assessed instant, while contact may occur anywhere during the blackout. The executable does not establish that credited contact occurred by that instant or addressed the urgency being assessed.
The test covers one firm and one STR. Its Boolean result cannot establish performance for all qualifying STRs.
Urgency classification and completion of urgent reporting remain unresolved; r2_completion is explicitly unencoded.
Schema conformity and liaison as soon as possible remain mandatory but unencoded: the performance child returned E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE.
The executable result determines current trigger satisfaction only; it does not determine compliance or discharge of previously triggered duties.
The bundle's valid_from date of 26 September 2026 is not a source-derived commencement date and does not establish coverage of earlier transition assessments.
The executable child formalizes only the trigger; the mandatory performance duty remains unencoded, so complete parent satisfaction cannot be computed.
The proposal retains the source's unspecified resubmission timing and linkage requirements as explicit residual questions.

The proposal adds an evidentiary requirement for time-of-day classification of implementation, which is a stated interpretation of the 9:00am launch boundary rather than a substantive change to the duty.

All three actual executable children are UNENCODED: the interval and follow-up children report E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE, and the contact child reports E_SCHEMA. Executable preservation is therefore unestablished.
The proposed Boolean urgency fact does not encode the exact clock-time interval or link an urgent submission event to that interval.
The proposed contact fact does not explicitly bind the contact to the same STR, its urgency, or the blackout interval; unrelated historical contact could satisfy an inadequately grounded valuation.
The licensed-firm actor, every applicable STR, direct contact, and specified contact destinations remain prose conditions without demonstrated executable enforcement.

The proposed implication returns true outside the urgency condition; this must mean inapplicability rather than substantive compliance. Its Boolean compliance label also does not independently preserve the source's should/please modality.
The prose retains uncertainty about completed filing and later follow-up, but no executable child preserves the separation between pre-launch contact and the post-implementation submission trigger.
Both actual children are UNENCODED with E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE; executable preservation of the parent's conditional assumptions and unresolved exception attachment cannot be verified.

The prose retains indivisibility and principal-economic-character treatment as conditional premises, but no supplied authority establishes either a dominance test or the legal consequences of separability.

The parent's explicit assessment that the competing reading is materially less supported is not expressly retained, although its lack of authority and inability to determine the exception remain explicit.
